things.title: Where does something new land in the factory?

options.name: A form on the Factory
options.difference: People type a request; it lands in To do as a card. Errors aren't covered.

options.name: One inbox, any source
options.difference: Requests, errors and GitHub issues all arrive as signals marked with where they came from; small ones can go straight to To do.

options.name: Errors straight to the board
options.difference: Each error becomes a card on the Factory board at once; requests are added by hand.

changes: Variant B ("One inbox, any source") only: move the Inbox off the Factory page and into the Signals page. Requests, errors from the factory and posts from the public feedback board appear in the ordinary Signals list, each with its source label (Request, Error, Feedback board, GitHub issue); a small filter at the top shows one source at a time. Keep "Straight to To do" for small ones and "Explore" for bigger ones on each signal. The Factory page goes back to just the board. Open it on the Signals page.

things.title: Send anywhere, use in the factory
things.diagram:
flowchart LR
  S1[Someone in any factory writes a wish or bug] --> P[They see exactly what will be sent]
  S2[The factory hits an error and offers to report it] --> P
  P --> G[It goes to the public feedback board, with their GitHub sign-in]
  G --> I[Our factory reads it into the inbox]
  I --> E[We explore it with the kobold]
  I --> T[Small ones go straight to To do]

things.title: How does an app send to the factory?

options.name: A ready-made Feedback button
options.difference: Any app adds a button the factory provides; needs something running online, which you don't have yet.

options.name: A drop-box address per product
options.difference: Any app sends to the product's own address; needs something running online, which you don't have yet.

options.name: GitHub, through a small free helper
options.difference: A tiny free online helper holds the key so people without access can send too; one setup step, something to look after.

options.name: Each sender's own GitHub sign-in
options.difference: Whoever sends is signed in to GitHub with access to the board (the factory already connects to GitHub); nothing to host.

options.name: A public feedback board
options.difference: A separate public GitHub repository just for feedback; anyone with a GitHub account sends from their factory, your code stays private, nothing to host.

things.text: Errors can carry a team's own data. Before anything is sent, the person sees exactly what goes out and can edit or remove it.

things.name: A public feedback board
things.difference: A separate public GitHub repository just for feedback; anyone with a GitHub account sends from their factory, your code stays private, nothing to host.

variants.name: A public feedback board
variants.difference: A separate public GitHub repository just for feedback; anyone with a GitHub account sends from their factory, your code stays private, nothing to host.

variants.name: Tell the kobold
variants.difference: No form. In the "Ask Sprocket anything" bar the person just says or types the wish or bug in their own words ("I wish I could…"). The kobold asks one or two short questions, finds similar posts on the public board ("3 teams want this too — add your 👍?"), writes a clean title and description, and shows the draft as a card with what goes along (version, page, errors with any team data highlighted to remove). One "Send" with their GitHub sign-in; afterwards it follows the post's state (sent, seen, planned, done) in the same chat. Errors still pop up as "Report this error", which opens this chat already filled in.

changes: Show the sending side, inside any factory: a "Send feedback" button always at hand (sidebar). It opens a short form: wish or bug, a title, a few words. When the factory hits an error, it offers "Report this error" with the details filled in. Before sending, the person sees exactly what will go out and can edit or remove any part (errors can carry their team's data). Sending uses their own GitHub sign-in and lands on a public feedback board on GitHub; afterwards they see a link to it there and its state later (seen, planned, done).

Variant F ("Tell the kobold") only; leave variant E as it is. F is too minimal: people don't know what to do. "Send feedback" in the sidebar (and "Report this error") opens a small, clean support window (a panel docked at the bottom right, not the tiny bar) with a header "Help & feedback". Before any chat, it shows three clear starting choices as tappable rows: "Something is wrong", "I wish Kobble could…", "Ask a question", plus a small "Your posts (2)" link showing their sent posts and states. Picking one starts the chat with Sprocket in that window with a matching first line and two or three example quick replies; the rest stays as it is (short questions, similar posts with 👍, draft card with what goes along and team data to remove, Send with GitHub sign-in, following the state). Keep it minimal: few words, lots of space, no form fields.

Variant F only; leave E as it is. Merge the two: no separate "Help & feedback" panel. Everything opens in the one Sprocket window: clicking "Ask Sprocket anything", "Send feedback" or "Report this error" makes the bar grow smoothly into the Sprocket window. Make that window feel alive rather than a static chat: (1) its opening adapts to where you are, e.g. on the Factory page "Builder stopped? Report it", plus the three starting choices (Something is wrong, I wish Kobble could…, Ask a question) as small chips, and a waiting error shows as the first suggestion; (2) while you talk, the post builds itself live in a card pinned at the top of the window (title, what happened, what goes along fill in and update as you answer), so you see the result taking shape instead of a wall of messages; (3) Sprocket's replies type in, with a short "thinking" moment, and quick replies change with each step; (4) similar posts slide in as you type, with 👍; (5) after Send the card turns into a small live status (sent → seen → planned → done) and "Your posts" is a tab in the window header. Keep it minimal and calm: few words, soft motion, no form fields.

Variant F only. (1) The Sprocket window must never open or grow by itself: remove the "opens on the first page of a visit" behaviour; it opens only when the person clicks "Ask Sprocket anything", "Send feedback" or "Report this error". (2) Remove "Your posts" from the Sprocket window (no tab, no link). Instead, the posts a person sent and their state (sent, seen, planned, done) live under the "Send feedback" entry in the sidebar: a small Feedback page/tab listing them, with a button there to send new feedback, which opens the Sprocket window.

Variant F only: the opening shows the same thing twice ("The builder stopped: git push… · Report it" and "Builder stopped? Report it"). Keep only one suggestion for a waiting error; the page-based hint shows only when there is no waiting error.

Variant F only, replacing the earlier "Feedback page under Send feedback" request: there is no separate Feedback page. The feedback a person sent, with its state (sent, seen, planned, done), shows on the Signals page, in a small "Feedback" section or filter, marked as sent to the public feedback board. In the factory that reads the board, posts arriving from it also land in Signals, marked "From the feedback board", like any other signal. "Your posts" stays out of the Sprocket window.

Variant F only. (1) The opening repeats itself: the header says "Sprocket", then a second Sprocket face with "Hi, I'm Sprocket. You're on Explorations. How can I help?". Keep Sprocket's face and name only once, in the header; the opening is just one short line, "How can I help?", and the page shows through the suggestions (e.g. on Factory "Builder stopped? Report it"), not through the words "You're on …". (2) Remove the "+" button from the header. Starting over only shows once a conversation has begun, as a small "Start over" text link. (3) As planned, sent feedback lives in the Signals list: each one is an ordinary signal with a "Feedback board" source label and a small state label (sent, seen, planned, done), and a "Feedback" filter at the top shows only those; feedback arriving from the board lands there the same way. No separate Feedback page.

Variant F only: on Signals, under "All", the feedback list shows above a separate big empty box ("No customers yet. Send your personas…"). Feedback should be part of the one Signals list, mixed in with the other signals by time; the empty box shows only when there are no signals at all.

Variant F only: on Signals, feedback posts arriving from the feedback board get a persona, matched by the kobold. Instead of the generic feedback icon, each shows the face of the product's persona it fits best (like the other signals do), with a small line in the detail: "Sprocket thinks this is <persona name>: <one short reason>", and a way to change or remove the persona if it's wrong. Posts the kobold isn't sure about keep the empty tile ("No persona yet"). Make up a mix: most matched, one left blank. The "Feedback board" source label and state stay as they are.

Variant F only: the team finds the Sprocket chat buggy, and the maker never saw it running. Open the Sprocket window yourself and click through every path from start to end: from "Ask Sprocket anything", "Send feedback" and "Report this error"; each of the three choices; the quick replies; the 👍 offer; the live card filling in; removing team data; Send; the status afterwards; "Start over"; closing and reopening. Fix anything that jumps, repeats, gets stuck, overlaps or grows oddly, and say what you fixed.

Variant F only: fix spacing issues. On Signals, the "Send more personas…" line sits right under the list and runs into the "Ask Sprocket anything" bar; leave room at the bottom of the page so nothing hides behind the bar. In the persona box in the detail, "Change" and "Remove" crowd the text; give them their own row with even space. Check the gaps in the Sprocket window too (header, suggestions, chips, live card, input) and in the sidebar error notice, so spacing matches the rest of Kobble's pages.

Variant F only: the Sprocket window still opens too tall, with an odd empty white space. When it opens, it should be only as tall as what it shows (header, "How can I help?", the suggestion, the chips, the input), with no empty area; it grows only as the conversation adds lines, up to a maximum height, then scrolls. Check it opened from "Ask Sprocket anything", "Send feedback" and "Report this error", and after "Start over".

things.title: Which persona does a feedback signal belong to?

options.name: The kobold matches it
options.difference: The kobold reads each post and puts the face of the persona it fits on it (e.g. the owner who isn't a developer); unsure ones stay blank.

options.name: The sender says who they are
options.difference: Sprocket asks one quick question when sending ("Are you the owner or a developer?"); the answer travels with the post and picks the persona.

options.name: No personas
options.difference: Feedback shows the sending team's name only, as now.

things.text: Before it goes live: the team creates the public feedback board on GitHub; the new words get Italian and German; Sprocket gets real thinking instead of the prototype's script.
